sections.title: Product Information
sections.description: FOM nanoRC product information: coating mechanics, control features, and lab-scale positioning.
body: The system deposits thin films from solution or slurry-based precursors onto flexible substrates, with a deposition length of 500 mm.
It's built to mimic the coating processes of large-scale roll-to-roll machines, giving a genuine miniaturized demonstration of industrial-scale slot-die coating rather than an approximation.

A touch display serves as the control panel, letting operators adjust drum speed, temperature, and rotation direction directly, with a physical power switch on the machine itself rather than a software-based one.
Key components include the touch display, a slot-die mounting gantry, adjustable feet, a removable drip tray, and a substrate support drum, with ventilation ducts and a power plug at the rear.
A drying system is built in, handling the deposited film as part of the coating process rather than requiring a separate step.
The machine doesn't come with an integrated syringe pump as standard, though FOM Technologies offers the option to combine the nanoRC with a compatible pump for precursor delivery.
Construction stays portable and compact, light enough to move around a lab, and the system is designed to run without scheduled maintenance or service.
It complies with the Machine Standards EN 60204-1 and ISO 13849-1 (CE), meeting the requirements of the 2006/42/EC Machinery Directive Annex II B.

sections.eyebrow: Replacing Spin Coating with Real Scalability
sections.title: Replacing Spin Coating with Real Scalability
sections.description: Spin coating is fast and familiar, but it answers a narrower question than most research programs actually need answered. Substrate size restraints, difficult batch processing, and a high percentage of material waste all limit how much a spin-coated result actually tells you about industrial viability. FOM nanoRC is built specifically to close that gap, replicating the coating process of large-scale roll-to-roll machines at laboratory scale, so results generated on the benchtop carry real, transferable relevance to pilot or production-scale coating lines. That makes it possible to develop or transfer thin-film knowledge directly into slot-die coating fabrication protocols, without the material consumption or hassle of a larger pilot line, while still supporting genuinely high-throughput experimental design.

sections.title: Machine Components and Control
sections.description: Every part of the coating process, from precursor delivery to the finished dried film, is handled through a small, purpose-built set of components.
body: The touch display sits at the center of daily operation, controlling drum speed, temperature, and rotation direction directly, with a physical power switch on the machine itself for turning the system on and off. The slot-die mounting gantry positions the coating head precisely over the substrate support drum, while a removable drip tray keeps runoff contained and cleanup simple between coating sessions. A built-in drying system processes the deposited film as part of the same workflow, and ventilation ducts at the rear manage airflow during operation. Because the system doesn't ship with an integrated syringe pump, FOM Technologies offers it as an optional combination, letting precursor delivery be matched to your specific formulation needs.

Automated documentation logs complete coating conditions through the control software, with the option to print alongside the coated area using a synchronized barcode printer/reader.
An integrated monitoring system with ethernet access supports easy service and remote troubleshooting.
Built on a new PLC platform, the system is Industry 4.0 ready and capable of industrial production speed, allowing facile reconfiguration once research is ready for technology transfer.
ATEX-compatible certification is available upon request.

sections.title: Building Your Production Line
sections.description: Industrial roll-to-roll equipment is usually built for one process and stays that way. FOM moduloR2R starts from the opposite assumption: that a research line needs to change as the research does. The base model, unwind, rewind, oven, and slot-die stations, handles simple pilot-scale thin film production immediately. From there, machine modules and process stations get added to customize and optimize the line for whatever coating process your work actually requires, including integrating entirely different deposition methods like flexographic, inkjet, or rotary screen printing alongside slot-die coating on the same frame. All-around web access keeps that expanded line maintainable and constantly monitorable, rather than becoming harder to service as it grows more complex.

sections.title: Data Management and Documentation
sections.description: Pilot-scale runs generate more data than manual documentation can realistically keep up with, and that's exactly the gap FOM moduloR2R's control software is built to close.
body: Complete coating conditions log automatically through the control software as a run proceeds, removing the need for manual record-keeping during production. Where physical traceability matters, that data can also print alongside the coated area itself using a synchronized barcode printer and reader, tying digital records directly to the physical film. Combined with process data export functions, that turns a pilot run into a genuinely analyzable dataset rather than a one-time production event.
